mainTopic: The eating time of the חגיגת ארבעה עשר, and when someone who slaughters a פסח on שבת with a wrong intent or a hidden problem must bring a חטאת.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about the חגיגת ארבעה עשר, the festival שלמים brought with the קרבן פסח. The ברייתא proves that this חגיגה may be eaten for two days and one night, first from the extra word 'לבקר' and then from the verse 'אם נדר או נדבה'. The גמרא asks why a second proof was needed. It explains that the ברייתא was considering a new reading: two separate חגיגות, each eaten for only a day and a night. That reading fails because it leaves 'אם נדר או נדבה' with no job. So that verse is assigned to the 15th's חגיגה, and the other verse teaches that the 14th's חגיגה also lasts two days and one night. The גמרא then concludes that a plain 'בקר' always means the first morning. A new משנה follows about slaughtering a פסח on שבת with the wrong intent. It includes a debate between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about other offerings slaughtered as a פסח, and רבי מאיר's report of how far רבי יהושע's exemption reaches. The משנה ends with cases of wrong owners, blemishes and hidden טריפות, exempting a slaughterer who acted ברשות.

steps.title: The fourteenth's חגיגה is eaten for two days and one night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the verse teaches the חגיגת ארבעה עשר may be eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse taught about the חגיגה of the fourteenth: it is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states what the verse 'ולא ילין... ביום הראשון לבקר' is teaching. The חגיגה brought on the 14th may be eaten for two days and one night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two days and one night means the day of the 14th, the night of the 15th, and the day of the 15th. The meat may not be left until the morning of the 16th. This is the same eating time as a regular שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival peace-offering brought on the 14th of ניסן together with the קרבן פסח
It taught (the verse teaches)
Two days and one night, the standard eating time of a שלמים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the קרבן פסח itself. The פסח may be eaten only that one night. This ruling is about the חגיגה brought alongside it.

phrases.english: It taught about the Festival offering of the fourteenth
that it is eaten for two days and one night.
phrases.notes: That is, until (but not including) the morning of the 16th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חגיגת ארבעה עשר may be eaten for two days and one night.

steps.title: Maybe it is only one day and one night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the חגיגה might be limited to only one day and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it is eaten only for a day and a night?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another possible reading: maybe the verse means only one day and one night. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the limit were one day and one night, the meat would have to be finished before the morning of the 15th. The ברייתא raises this option so it can show from the wording of the verse that it is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only…; the ברייתא's way of raising another possible reading
A day and a night (the shorter eating time)

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only for a day and a night?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Could the verse be setting a shorter limit of one day and one night?

steps.title: The extra word 'until the morning' points to the second morning
steps.stepSummary: The verse adds 'לבקר' after 'ביום הראשון', so it must mean the second morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the verse says 'on the first day... until the morning', that is speaking of the second morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the exact words of the verse. The extra word 'לבקר' shows the limit is the second morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah meant only the first morning, 'ביום הראשון' alone would be enough. Adding 'לבקר' points to a later morning, the morning after the 15th. So the meat may be eaten until the morning of the 16th.

keyTerms.meaning: When it (the verse) says; introduces a proof from the verse
The second morning (the morning of the 16th)
Here it is stated / it is already said

phrases.english: When it says: 'on the first day... until the morning' —
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in דברים 16:4.

phrases.english: the second morning is being stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'לבקר' shows the limit is the second morning, so it is two days and one night.

steps.title: Maybe this חגיגה is an exception to the usual rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that maybe it is only the first morning, and the usual two-day rule for חגיגה applies to other חגיגות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is only the first morning. And how do I keep the rule that a חגיגה is eaten for two days and one night? That applies to every חגיגה except this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back again. Maybe the limit really is the first morning, and the well-known two-day rule simply does not apply to this particular חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge admits there is a general rule that a חגיגה lasts two days and one night. It suggests the חגיגה of the 14th could be an exception with a shorter time. This would still be a חגיגה; only its eating time would be different.

keyTerms.meaning: And how do I fulfill / explain (the other teaching)?
Except for this one
The first morning (the morning of the 15th)

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only the first morning,
and how do I uphold

phrases.english: that a Festival offering is eaten for two days and one night —
for all except this one,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the חגיגת ארבעה עשר lasts until the second morning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general two-day rule could hold for other חגיגות, while this one is an exception limited to the first morning.

steps.title: Proof from 'if it is a vow or a free-will offering'
steps.stepSummary: The verse about שלמים, 'אם נדר או נדבה', teaches that the חגיגת ארבעה עשר is also eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says about it 'if it is a vow or a free-will offering', it teaches that the חגיגה of the fourteenth is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a second verse, from the laws of שלמים. That verse shows the חגיגה of the 14th also gets two days and one night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא 7:16 gives שלמים two days ('on the day... and on the morrow'). The ברייתא uses it to show that the 14th's חגיגה also gets two days, which cancels the idea that it is an exception. Steps 8–9 explain exactly how this proof works.

keyTerms.meaning: A vowed offering
A free-will offering

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר בּוֹ: ״אִם נֶדֶר אוֹ נְדָבָה״ —
phrases.english: When it says regarding it: 'if it is a vow or a free-will offering' —
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא 7:16.

phrases.english: it taught about the Festival offering of the fourteenth

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר בּוֹ אִם נֶדֶר אוֹ נְדָבָה

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the חגיגה of the 14th is an exception limited to one night.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse 'אם נדר או נדבה' includes it in the two-day rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא ends with two proofs that the חגיגת ארבעה עשר lasts two days and one night: the extra word 'לבקר' and the verse 'אם נדר או נדבה'.

steps.title: Why raise 'the first morning' after the verse already proved the second morning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא could suggest 'the first morning' when it already proved the verse means the second morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Or perhaps it is only the first morning.' But you already said that when the verse says 'on the first day... until the morning', it speaks of the second morning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now examines the ברייתא itself. It asks why the ברייתא went back to the 'first morning' idea, since that idea was already disproved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from 'לבקר' already ruled out the first morning. So the ברייתא's second suggestion looks like it repeats a rejected idea. That seems to make the second proof unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; the גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא in order to discuss it
But you already said!

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בֹּקֶר רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: The Master said: Or perhaps it is only the first morning.
But you already said:
when it says 'on the first day (until the morning)' —
the second morning is being stated?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בֹּקֶר רִאשׁוֹן הָא אָמַרְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא steps back to analyze the ברייתא's flow.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's suggestion of 'the first morning' in step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 3 already proved from 'לבקר' that the verse means the second morning, so the suggestion is already disproved.

steps.title: The suggestion was really about two different חגיגות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא meant: maybe the verse speaks of two חגיגות, the 14th's and the 15th's, each eaten only until its own morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: Or perhaps the verse is speaking about two Festival offerings, one the חגיגה of the fourteenth and one the חגיגה of the fifteenth, and each is eaten until its own morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reexplains the ברייתא's second suggestion. It was not repeating the rejected idea. It was offering a new way to read the word 'second morning'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this new reading, 'second morning' can still be true. The 14th's חגיגה ends the morning of the 15th. The 15th's חגיגה ends the morning of the 16th, which is the 'second morning'. So the word 'לבקר' would not prove that the 14th's חגיגה lasts two days.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying; introduces a reinterpretation
The festival offering brought on the 15th of ניסן
This one until its morning and that one until its morning

steps.confusionAlert: Under this reading, the 'second morning' is the morning of the 16th, but it belongs to the 15th's חגיגה, not to the 14th's.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁתֵּי חֲגִיגוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: Or perhaps the verse is speaking only of two Festival offerings,
one the Festival offering of the fourteenth
and one the Festival offering of the fifteenth,
and this one until its morning and that one until its morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was simply repeating the already-rejected 'first morning' idea.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא raised a new reading: two חגיגות, each eaten for one day and one night, which explains 'second morning' in a different way.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why the second proof, 'אם נדר או נדבה', was needed. The first proof could be explained away.

steps.title: Which offering could 'vow or free-will offering' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: since a חגיגה is known to last two days and one night, the verse 'אם נדר או נדבה' cannot be about the 14th's or the 15th's חגיגה under the new reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: It then says: But we hold that a חגיגה is eaten for two days and one night. If so, what is 'if it is a vow or a free-will offering' talking about? If it is the חגיגה of the fourteenth, it is written that it lasts a day and a night! If it is the חגיגה of the fifteenth, it is written that it lasts a day and a night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא's proof from 'אם נדר או נדבה' works against the two-חגיגות reading. It shows that, under that reading, the verse would not fit either חגיגה. The argument continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We hold that a חגיגה can last two days and one night, and that rule comes from 'אם נדר או נדבה'. But under the two-חגיגות reading, both the 14th's and the 15th's חגיגה would be limited to a day and a night, so that verse would have no חגיגה left to apply to. The next step resolves this: 'אם נדר או נדבה' is assigned to the 15th's חגיגה, which leaves the other verse wholly about the 14th's.

keyTerms.meaning: It then says (the ברייתא continues its argument)
That which we hold as established
About what (case)?
But it is written about it!

phrases.english: It then says:
But that which we hold

phrases.aramaic: חֲגִיגָה הַנֶּאֱכֶלֶת לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וָלַיְלָה אֶחָד.
phrases.english: that a Festival offering is eaten for two days and one night —

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן: ״אִם נֶדֶר אוֹ נְדָבָה״ בְּמַאי?
phrases.english: if so, 'if it is a vow or a free-will offering' — about what is it speaking?
If the Festival offering of the fourteenth,
surely it is written about it: a day and a night!
phrases.notes: This fits the reading where there are two חגיגות.

phrases.english: If the Festival offering of the fifteenth,
surely it is written about it: a day and a night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the proof from 'אם נדר או נדבה' (step 5) works against the two-חגיגות reading of step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the חגיגת ארבעה עשר is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:16, 'אם נדר או נדבה', which must apply to some חגיגה but fits neither one under the two-חגיגות reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two-חגיגות reading of step 7, in which each חגיגה is eaten only for a day and a night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the verse 'אם נדר או נדבה', which gives a חגיגה two days and one night, would fit neither the 14th's nor the 15th's חגיגה.

steps.title: The 14th's חגיגה lasts two days and one night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the verse 'אם נדר או נדבה' refers to the חגיגת חמשה עשר. The other verse refers entirely to the חגיגת ארבעה עשר, which teaches that it is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this verse (about a vow or free-will offering) is about the חגיגה of the 15th. That other verse is entirely about the חגיגה of the 14th. It teaches that the חגיגה of the 14th is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its argument and gives its final reading of the two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that the 'two separate חגיגות' reading leaves the verse 'אם נדר או נדבה' with no job. So the ברייתא assigns that verse to the 15th's חגיגה. The other verse ('לא ילין... לבקר') then refers wholly to the 14th's חגיגה, which means it too is eaten for two days and one night.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival peace-offering brought on the 15th of ניסן
The entire verse
It taught
Two days and the one night between them

steps.whatToRemember: Final conclusion of the ברייתא: the חגיגת ארבעה עשר, like any שלמים, may be eaten for two days and one night.

phrases.english: Rather, this verse is for the Festival offering of the fifteenth,
and that other verse, all of it,
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק 'ולא ילין מן הבשר... לבקר'.

phrases.english: is for the Festival offering of the fourteenth;

that it is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that follows from the proof in Step 8
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The verse 'אם נדר או נדבה' is about the 15th's חגיגה. The other verse is about the 14th's חגיגה, which is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.title: An unspecified 'morning' means the first morning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its own discussion. The verse needed the words 'ביום הראשון' to push 'morning' to the second morning. This shows that a plain 'בקר' always means the first morning, even without the word 'first.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason we know it means a later morning is that the verse says 'on the first day... until morning.' What morning is that? The second morning. This shows that wherever 'morning' is written plainly, it means the first morning, even though the word 'first' is not written with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the ברייתא and draws a general rule from it about the word 'בקר.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could only mean 'the second morning' because of the added words 'ביום הראשון.' So a plain 'בקר' must automatically mean the first morning that comes after the offering. That makes the earlier derivation (רב כהנא's), which relied on the word 'first,' unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is because it is written
The second morning
Plainly, with no qualifier
'First,' the word one might have thought was needed

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'ביום הראשון' does not mean 'morning' is the first morning. Here it is what pushes the meaning to the SECOND morning. Without such words, 'morning' means the first morning.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general reading rule. A plain 'בקר' in the תורה refers to the very next morning.

phrases.english: The reason is that it is written: 'on the first day... until the morning,'
so that 'morning' means: the second morning.

phrases.aramaic: הָא כׇּל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב בֹּקֶר סְתָמָא
phrases.english: This implies that wherever 'morning' is written unspecified,
it means the first morning,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא כְּתַב בֵּיהּ ״רֵאשִׁית״.
phrases.english: even though 'first' is not written with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's final reading to draw a general inference about the word 'בקר'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A plain 'בקר' means the first morning. No extra word 'first' is needed to teach this.

steps.title: New משנה: a פסח slaughtered for the wrong purpose on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who slaughters a קרבן פסח שלא לשמו on שבת is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A פסח that someone slaughtered for a different purpose on שבת: he is liable to bring a חטאת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. If someone slaughters a פסח on שבת with the wrong intent, he has broken שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a פסח is normally allowed on שבת because it is a מצוה. When it is done שלא לשמו, the offering becomes invalid as a פסח, so no מצוה was done. The slaughter is then simply a forbidden מלאכה done by mistake, which requires a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Not for its own sake, i.e., with intent for a different offering
A sin-offering brought for an accidental sin
Liable

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A Paschal offering that one slaughtered not for its own sake
on Shabbat: he is liable to bring a sin-offering for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַפֶּסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering a פסח שלא לשמו on שבת makes one liable for a חטאת.

steps.title: Other offerings slaughtered on שבת as a פסח
steps.stepSummary: If other offerings are slaughtered on שבת for the sake of a פסח and they are unfit to be a פסח, the person is liable. If they are fit, רבי אליעזר holds him liable for a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all other offerings that someone slaughtered for the sake of a פסח: if they are not fit to be a פסח, he is liable. If they are fit, רבי אליעזר holds him liable for a חטאת, and רבי יהושע exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the reverse case. Here a different offering is slaughtered on שבת as if it were a פסח. It records a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal could never be a פסח (for example, a female or an animal from the herd), the mistake is obvious. The slaughter was simply a forbidden act, so the person is liable. If the animal is the right kind, רבי אליעזר still holds him liable. רבי יהושע exempts him, because he set out to do a מצוה and an offering slaughtered for the wrong purpose is still valid, so in the end a מצוה was done.

keyTerms.meaning: All other offerings
For the sake of a פסח
Fit (the right kind of animal to be a פסח)
Exempts

steps.whatToRemember: An unfit animal makes the person liable according to everyone. With a fit animal, רבי אליעזר says liable and רבי יהושע says exempt.

phrases.english: And all other offerings
that one slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering:
if they are not fit, he is liable;
and if they are fit,
Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to bring a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר כׇּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the reverse case: other offerings slaughtered as a פסח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the animal is unfit to be a פסח, the person is liable. If it is fit, this is a מחלוקת: רבי אליעזר holds him liable and רבי יהושע exempts him.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's logical argument for liability
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues from the פסח to other offerings. If changing a פסח's purpose on שבת makes one liable, then changing other offerings' purpose should surely make one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: Look at the פסח. It is allowed to be slaughtered on שבת for its own purpose. Yet if someone changed its purpose, he is liable. Other offerings are not allowed to be slaughtered on שבת even for their own purpose. So when someone changes their purpose, isn't it logical that he should be liable?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר is defending his ruling from the משנה with a logical argument. He says that someone who slaughters other offerings as a פסח on שבת must bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר, an argument from a lenient case to a strict one. The פסח is the lenient case, because it may be slaughtered on שבת. Even so, changing its purpose makes one liable. Other offerings may not be slaughtered on שבת at all, so changing their purpose should make one liable even more.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lenient case to a stricter case
For its own purpose (as the offering it really is)
He changed its purpose (slaughtered it as a different offering)
Other animal offerings
Is it not logical? (introduces the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אִם הַפֶּסַח שֶׁהוּא מוּתָּר לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: If the Pesach, which is permitted on Shabbat for its own purpose,
phrases.notes: The lenient side of the argument

phrases.english: when he changed its purpose, he is liable,
phrases.notes: This is the ruling from Step 11

phrases.english: then other offerings, which are forbidden on Shabbat even for their own purpose,
when he changed their purpose,
is it not logical that he should be liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אִם הַפֶּסַח שֶׁהוּא מוּתָּר לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אליעזר's position from Step 12 with a קל וחומר
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that one who slaughters fit offerings as a פסח on שבת is liable
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the ruling that a פסח slaughtered for a different purpose on שבת makes one liable

steps.title: רבי יהושע rejects the comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the cases are different. A פסח was changed into something forbidden on שבת. Other offerings were changed into a פסח, which is permitted on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No. You can say this about the פסח, because he changed it into something forbidden. Can you say it about other offerings, which he changed into something permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע knocks down רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר. He points out a real difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a פסח is slaughtered as a different offering, it becomes an offering that may not be brought on שבת. That is why he is liable. When other offerings are slaughtered as a פסח, they become a פסח, which may be brought on שבת. His mistake was toward a permitted act, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: No. If you say [this in case A]... (the standard way to reject a קל וחומר)
Something forbidden (here, an offering not allowed on שבת)
Something permitted (here, the פסח, which is allowed on שבת)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No,
if you say this about the Pesach,
it is because he changed it into something forbidden,
phrases.notes: Other individual offerings are not brought on שבת

phrases.english: will you say the same about other offerings
that he changed into something permitted?
phrases.notes: The פסח may be slaughtered on שבת

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר from Step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר of רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases are not alike. The פסח was changed into a forbidden offering, while the other offerings were changed into a permitted one.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brings proof from communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר shows a case where changing an offering into something permitted still makes one liable. That case is slaughtering for the sake of communal offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: Let the communal offerings prove it. They are permitted on שבת for their own purpose, and yet someone who slaughters another animal for their purpose is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע's objection with a counterexample. He shows that even an offering "changed into something permitted" can still make one liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings, like the תמיד and the מוסף, may be brought on שבת. Even so, if someone slaughters an extra animal for their sake, he is liable. This seems to break רבי יהושע's rule that changing toward something permitted makes one exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offerings (like the תמיד and the מוסף), which may be brought on שבת
Let them prove it (introduces a counterexample)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: אֵימוּרֵי צִיבּוּר יוֹכִיחוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: Let communal offerings prove it,
for they are permitted on Shabbat for their own purpose,
and yet one who slaughters another animal for their purpose is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רבי יהושע's distinction from Step 14
steps.raayaObject: That changing an offering into something permitted still makes one liable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law that slaughtering another animal for the sake of אימורי ציבור on שבת makes one liable

steps.title: רבי יהושע rejects the proof: communal offerings have a fixed number
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says communal offerings are different because their number is fixed. The פסח has no fixed number, so a mistake there is understandable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No. You can say this about communal offerings, because they have a fixed limit. Can you say it about the פסח, which has no limit?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back on רבי אליעזר's counterexample. He explains why communal offerings are not a good comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings have a set number each day, so slaughtering an extra one is a careless act with no excuse. A פסח has no limit, since any group may bring one. So mistakenly treating an animal as a פסח is an understandable error made while trying to do a מצוה, and he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed limit or set number
Will you say [the same about the other case]? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No,
if you say this about communal offerings,
it is because they have a fixed limit,
will you say the same about the Pesach, which has no limit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from אימורי ציבור in Step 15
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Communal offerings have a fixed number, so an extra one has no excuse. A פסח has no limit, so the error is understandable.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that one who slaughters fit offerings as a פסח on שבת is liable. רבי יהושע exempts him, because a פסח is permitted on שבת and has no fixed limit, so his mistake is a reasonable one.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: even for the sake of communal offerings he is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that even someone who slaughters an animal for the sake of communal offerings is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Even someone who slaughters for the sake of communal offerings is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר reports how far רבי יהושע's view goes. According to רבי יהושע, even slaughtering for the sake of communal offerings, the very case רבי אליעזר used as proof, makes one exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר assumed that slaughtering for the sake of אימורי ציבור makes one liable. According to רבי מאיר, רבי יהושע did not accept even that premise: there too one is exempt, because he meant to do a מצוה that is permitted on שבת. This undercuts רבי אליעזר's proof from its foundation.

keyTerms.meaning: Even (extends a ruling to a further case)
Exempt (not obligated to bring a חטאת)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם אֵימוּרֵי צִיבּוּר — פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: Even one who slaughters for the sake of communal offerings is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that, in רבי יהושע's view, the premise of רבי אליעזר's proof in Step 15 is itself wrong
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering on שבת for the sake of אימורי ציבור also makes one exempt

steps.title: A פסח slaughtered only for people who cannot eat it
steps.stepSummary: If a פסח is slaughtered on שבת only for people who cannot eat it or are not registered for it, or only for people who are uncircumcised or impure, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it for people who cannot eat it and for people not registered for it, or for uncircumcised or impure people, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case. It asks what happens when a פסח is slaughtered on שבת for the wrong people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח slaughtered only for people who cannot eat it, or who are not signed up for it, is invalid. The same is true for people who are uncircumcised or impure. Since the slaughtering produced an invalid offering, it was a needless act of work on שבת, so he must bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: For people who cannot eat it (for example, the sick or elderly)
For people not registered for this פסח
Uncircumcised men, who may not eat the פסח
Ritually impure people
Liable (here, to bring a חטאת)

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it for those who cannot eat it
and for those not registered for it,
or for the uncircumcised and for the impure, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה opens a new set of cases about wrong intent on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered on שבת only for people who cannot eat it, are not registered, are uncircumcised, or are impure is invalid, so the slaughterer is liable

steps.title: A פסח slaughtered for a mix of fit and unfit people
steps.stepSummary: If the פסח was slaughtered for a mix of fit and unfit people, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it for those who can eat it and those who cannot, for those registered and those not registered, for the circumcised and the uncircumcised, or for the impure and the pure, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. Here the slaughterer intended the פסח for both fit and unfit people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When at least some of the people intended are fit, the פסח stays valid. Since a valid פסח may be slaughtered on שבת, his act was allowed. So he does not need to bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Circumcised men
Ritually pure people

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that mentioning unfit people always ruins the פסח. It only becomes invalid if it is slaughtered entirely for unfit people. A mix of fit and unfit people keeps it valid.
steps.whatToRemember: Only unfit people: the פסח is invalid and he is liable. A mix of fit and unfit people: the פסח is valid and he is exempt.

phrases.english: For those who can eat it and those who cannot eat it,
for those registered for it and those not registered for it,
for the circumcised and for the uncircumcised,
for the impure and for the pure, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to Step 18, where the intent is mixed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח slaughtered for a mix of fit and unfit people is valid, so the slaughterer is exempt

steps.title: Visible blemish makes him liable, hidden defect makes him exempt
steps.stepSummary: If the פסח slaughtered on שבת turns out to be a בעל מום, the slaughterer is חייב. If it turns out to be a טריפה בסתר, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it and it turned out to have a blemish, he is liable. If he slaughtered it and it turned out to be a טריפה because of a hidden defect, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two cases where the פסח turns out to be unfit after it was slaughtered on שבת. It gives opposite rulings for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish (מום) can be seen from the outside, so he should have checked before slaughtering. That makes his act a careless mistake (שוגג), and he needs a חטאת. A hidden טריפה could not have been found even with a proper check, so his act counts as an unavoidable accident (אונס), and he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a physical blemish that disqualifies it as an offering
An animal with a fatal defect that disqualifies it
Hidden, internal, and not visible from outside
Liable, here meaning he must bring a חטאת for breaking שבת by mistake
Exempt from bringing a חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: Both animals are unfit as a פסח. The difference is not whether the offering is disqualified, since both are. The difference is only whether the slaughterer could have known beforehand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key principle for this משנה: a mistake you could have avoided by checking is a שוגג, while a mistake nobody could have avoided is an אונס.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and it was found to have a blemish, he is liable.
phrases.notes: He should have checked for a visible blemish.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and it was found to be a tereifa with a hidden defect, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: No check could have revealed it, so it counts as an unavoidable accident.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of rulings in the משנה. The earlier cases were about whom the פסח was slaughtered for. Now the cases are about defects found in the animal itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Visible blemish (מום): liable. Hidden טריפה: exempt.

steps.title: Owners withdrew, died, or became impure: exempt because he slaughtered with permission
steps.stepSummary: If it later turns out that the owners had withdrawn from the פסח, died, or become impure, the slaughterer is פטור, because he slaughtered בִּרְשׁוּת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it and then it became known that the owners had withdrawn from it, or had died, or had become impure, he is exempt, because he slaughtered with permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third kind of case. Here the animal is fine, but the owners could no longer take part. It rules that the slaughterer is exempt, and it states the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment of slaughter he had every reason to think the פסח was valid, and nothing he could have checked would have told him otherwise. Because he acted with full permission (ברשות), this is not counted as a careless violation of שבת. Notice that this is the first time in the list that the משנה states its reason outright.

keyTerms.meaning: They withdrew their hands, meaning they left the group registered for this פסח
The owners, meaning the people registered for the offering
They became ritually impure
With permission, acting properly according to what was known at the time

steps.whatToRemember: The rule behind this whole section: if the slaughterer could have known by checking (a blemish), he is liable. If he could not have known (a hidden טריפה, or owners who withdrew, died, or became impure), he is exempt, because he slaughtered ברשות.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 18. There, he himself intended the פסח for people who could not eat it, which made the offering invalid, so he is liable. Here, he did not know and could not have known that the owners had dropped out, so he is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of ברשות explains all the exemptions in this משנה. It also connects to a larger question: is a mistake that could not be avoided still counted as a שוגג that needs a חטאת?

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and it became known
phrases.notes: The information came out only after the slaughter.

phrases.english: that the owners had withdrawn from it,
phrases.notes: They had registered for a different פסח, so no one was registered for this one.

phrases.english: or that they had died, or had become impure,
he is exempt, because he slaughtered with permission.
phrases.notes: The משנה states its reason directly here.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטוֹ וְנוֹדַע שֶׁמָּשְׁכוּ הַבְּעָלִים אֶת יָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same idea as the hidden-טריפה case to problems with the owners, and gives the reason in so many words: ברשות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the owners turn out to have withdrawn, died, or become impure, the slaughterer is exempt, because he slaughtered with permission.
